title: Deeply nested empty chains: three keys from a document with no leaves at all
rationale: The "flattens to more keys than it has leaves" case. Nested empty containers produce a key each and contribute zero scalar leaves, and this exercises empty chains at three different depths in one document.
catchesBugClass: Key-count accounting that assumes keys track leaves, plus regression of the depth-preservation property at more than one level. It would also catch a fix that drops empty chains entirely to save keys.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the far worse CELL blowup from array-of-maps. It also cannot distinguish {} from [] from null anywhere, so it keeps passing under any fix that addresses only one of the three.

predicted.detail: Zero leaves in, three keys out. Depth is preserved exactly - the already-pinned ACCEPTED behaviour - but every {} became null, the already-pinned DEFECT, now shown to propagate at every depth.
